items.content: “The chance of human extinction is about a coin flip, in my view,” Geoffrey Irving, a former OpenAI and Google DeepMind employee, said in a new interview. It’s one of a dozen interviews with AI researchers, including current and former employees at OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. Palisade Research, which says it’s a nonprofit studying AIs’ capabilities and motivations, collected and launched the interviews on frominside.ai.Several of the researchers joined Irving in warning about the possibility AI could drive humans extinct. Neel Nanda, a Google DeepMind research scientist, said there’s “at least a 10 percent chance that it causes human extinction, and that is ridiculously high.” We noted comments from both Nanda and Irving in a recent report about the “AI safety” community, and how difficult it is to nail down what that term means, or what anyone should do about it, and even these videos don’t have one cohesive solution to offer.RelatedWe’re running out of reasons to ignore AI safetyInside the suddenly explosive world of AI safetyFormer OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo went as far as claiming that superintelligent AI “would basically be god-like powerful,” and added, “unfortunately we don’t know how to control them at all. And so probably nobody would control them. This is exactly as dangerous as it sounds and must not be allowed to happen.”While each video is available in full, the site also collects segments from multiple people speaking on similar topics, including whether this is all just hype or marketing, and why they would work on something that they believe is this dangerous. Some of the responses include Google’s Mary Phuong saying “I think you absolutely should be suspicious of what I’m saying because I am being paid by the lab,” and Nanda’s explanation that “If I did not believe that my work was directly reducing these existential risks, I would quit… These companies are not going to stop making these systems just because I quit.”
items.author: Stevie Bonifield
items.titleZh: AI研究人员发布视频称超级智能“危险程度恰如其名”
items.descriptionZh:
前OpenAI和Google DeepMind员工杰弗里·欧文（Geoffrey Irving）在接受采访时称，在他看来，人类因AI而灭绝的概率“大约像掷硬币”，即约一半。这是Palisade Research在frominside.ai发布的一系列AI研究员访谈之一。Palisade自称非营利组织，研究AI的能力与动机；访谈对象有十几位，包括OpenAI、Google和Anthropic的现任及前任员工。多名受访者与欧文一样警告AI可能导致人类灭绝。Google DeepMind研究科学家尼尔·南达（Neel Nanda）说，AI造成人类灭绝的概率“至少10%，这高得离谱”。相关报道也提到，AI安全社区内部对“AI安全”的定义、该做什么缺乏共识，这些视频同样没有给出统一答案。

前OpenAI研究员丹尼尔·科科塔伊洛（Daniel Kokotajlo）称，超级智能AI“基本上会像神一样强大”，而人类“根本不知道如何控制它们”，“所以很可能没人能控制它们。这正和听起来一样危险，绝不能被允许发生”。从技术层面看，这组访谈的核心并非新模型或算法创新，而是AI安全中的控制/对齐难题：当系统能力远超人类时，如何保证其受控。网站除完整视频外，还按主题汇集多人发言，讨论这些警告是否只是炒作或营销，以及他们为何要从事自己认为如此危险的工作。

对于利益冲突，Google的玛丽·芳（Mary Phuong）说：“你绝对应该怀疑我说的话，因为我拿实验室的工资。”南达则解释：“如果我不相信我的工作能直接降低这些存在性风险，我会辞职……但这些公司不会因为我辞职就停止制造这些系统。”文章关联内容还指出，人们越来越没有理由忽视AI安全，AI安全领域突然成为热点，但其含义、责任和解决方案仍高度模糊。

items.title: Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond
items.description: How close is AI to designing the very same chips it runs on? We explore how artificial intelligence is being used in modern chip design today.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter In late August, Architect Labs claimed it had designed a chip that was almost entirely developed by AI, an industry-first achievement. AI is already used to optimize floorplans, placement and routing, verification, and other stages of semiconductor development. Generative AI can assist engineers with RTL code, whereas emerging agentic systems can operate electronic design automation (EDA) tools, analyze results, identify problems, modify designs, and repeat the process with increasingly less human intervention. Meanwhile, human engineers still define and develop architectures and make fundamental design decisions that determine what a chip does and how it works.This creates a curious feedback loop. Today's AI models run on processors designed by human engineers with growing assistance from AI; those models can then help design more capable processors for the next generation of AI systems. As EDA vendors and semiconductor companies give AI control over progressively larger portions of the design process, the industry is gradually moving from humans using AI tools to design chips toward AI systems participating in the design of the hardware on which their successors will run.Can machines indeed design machines today? Probably not. But will they be able to do so in the future? That's a big question with important ramifications — and engineers have been pondering it for longer than you might think.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: A brief history of AI in chip developmentCadence, Synopsys, and Siemens EDA, all leading developers of EDA software, alongside Ansys — a leading designer of simulation software — rolled out AI-enhanced versions of their tools in the early 2020s, before the generative AI boom took the world by storm. (Image credit: Synopsys)The first generation of AI-enhanced EDA software primarily used machine learning (ML) and reinforcement learning (RL) to tackle well-defined optimization problems. Given an existing design, a set of constraints, and particular targets, these tools could explore numerous implementation options to optimize placement and routing, and therefore power, performance, and area (PPA), while shrinking development time. Essentially, AI could find a better way to implement a design, but the design itself and its goals were still defined by engineers. You may like Hot Chips 2026: OpenAI's Jalapeño AI ASIC unpacked OpenAI Jalapeño design interview transcript Synopsys debuts Autopilot platform for developing chips autonomously using AI One of the key advantages of these tools was their ability to learn from previous runs and use accumulated data to guide subsequent design-space exploration, something which could reduce the number of iterations needed to meet PPA targets and, in some cases, produce results that would have required considerably more engineering time using conventional methods. Yet the autonomy of these tools is limited, as engineers define constraints, configure flows, run individual tools, analyze their output, and decide what to try next. AI accelerates or optimizes particular stages of chip development, but humans still control the overall design flow. And that's changing with newer generations.The latest AI-enhanced EDA tools are considerably more ambitious. Generative AI can write or modify RTL and verification code, analyze reports, identify potential points of failure, and even suggest fixes. Meanwhile, emerging agentic systems can operate multiple EDA tools and execute sequences of engineering tasks with very limited human intervention. Such an agent can analyze results, modify a design or its parameters, launch another simulation or implementation run, evaluate the outcome, and repeat the process until it reaches specified targets. As a result, AI is gradually moving from optimizing individual steps inside EDA tools to automating parts of the chip development workflow itself.From big bang to architecturesIn 2023 – 2024, both Cadence and Synopsys announced that hundreds of chip designs have been completed using their AI-enhanced Cadence.ai DSO.ai/VSO.ai/TSO.ai tools. Moreover, leading high-tech companies revealed details about how they used AI to complete their projects. Yet putting Google, Nvidia, OpenAI, and Architect Labs into the same bucket is not right, as they represent different degrees of AI involvement in chip development. (Image credit: Google Deepmind)Google, which was among the first high-tech giants to announce the use of AI to develop its AI accelerators, seems to be the least radical. Google's AlphaChip uses reinforcement learning mostly for physical floorplanning: it places circuit blocks and optimizes layouts, but it does not invent the entire design or the architecture itself. Google DeepMind said in 2024 that AlphaChip had been used for the previous three generations of TPUs, meaning Google was well ahead of the general EDA industry with its tools. (The company has not shared AlphaChip's progress in detail since then.)Nvidia is more interesting because its internal AI systems tend to automate work traditionally performed by hardware engineers. The important distinction is that Nvidia trains specialized models on its own RTL, documentation, and unique accumulated engineering knowledge, something a merchant EDA vendor cannot access. This makes Nvidia an example of a chip designer that turns the engineering data behind its proprietary GPU and, more recently, AI accelerator, CPU, DPU, and network cards into training data for AI. Nonetheless, Nvidia itself draws a clear line between its automation and autonomous chip design. What to read next Anthropic co-designing custom AI inference chips to bypass costly Nvidia GPUs OpenAI says its next-generation processors could be made at Samsung Hot Chips 2026: Cerebras lays out the future of wafer-scale AI OpenAI's Jalapeño is probably the strongest real-silicon example we currently have. OpenAI says AI was directly involved in implementation, design-space exploration, verification loops, and arithmetic-circuit optimization, which enabled the company to go from initial design to tapeout in nine months. At Hot Chips, OpenAI disclosed some concrete PPA advantages: Compared with human baselines, AI-assisted designs improved a BF16 multiplier by 56%, an FP4 dot-product block by 21%, and an FP32 accumulator by 10%, while reducing the area of matrix and SIMD units by 10% and 8%, respectively.OpenAI has not said that AI invented Jalapeño's architecture, so humans have indeed remained responsible for it. But AI was extensively used to turn that architecture into silicon and optimize it ... which brings us to Architect Labs.Indeed, Architect Labs' Redwood is qualitatively different. Two human architects defined the specification, after which Architect Labs says its AI autonomously generated and verified the logic, generated RTL, verified it, and produced firmware. To top it off, AI also assisted software development, including drivers and kernels. Meanwhile, unlike Google, Nvidia, and OpenAI, the company explicitly describes its system as one that performs machine learning co-design and says it can explore architectures, though without elaboration.Redwood was 'produced' in under two weeks and runs billion-plus-parameter models, but there is a huge caveat: It has not been taped out. It has never actually been produced as an ASIC; the accelerator runs on an FPGA, and the claimed 3.4X performance-per-watt advantage over Nvidia's Jetson Orin Nano is based on a projected Samsung 8LPP design.Final wordsJust a few years ago, AI in semiconductor development was largely an optimization technology that helped engineers find better ways to implement designs created by humans. Today, it can generate RTL, verify designs, operate EDA tools, and even explore architectural choices, although humans still define what ultimately gets built.We are therefore considerably closer to machines designing machines, but nowhere near the singularity quite yet. For now, chips are helping design their successors. But they aren't even close to deciding what those successors should be.
items.author: Anton Shilov
items.titleZh: 硅开始设计硅——人工智能如何从EDA工具到OpenAI的Jalapeño乃至更广领域应用于芯片制造
items.descriptionZh:
8月底，Architect Labs 宣称其设计了一款几乎完全由 AI 开发的芯片，并称这是业界首次。围绕这一事件，文章指出 AI 在芯片开发中的角色正从辅助优化走向更深入参与。AI 早已用于优化芯片的 Floorplan、布局布线、验证等环节；生成式 AI 可帮助编写 RTL 代码；新兴的 agentic 系统则可操作 EDA 工具、分析结果、发现问题、修改设计并反复迭代，人工干预越来越少。但人类工程师仍负责定义架构和决定芯片功能与工作方式。由此形成反馈循环：今天的 AI 模型运行在人类工程师借助 AI 设计的处理器上，这些模型又能帮助设计下一代 AI 系统所需的更强处理器。随着 EDA 厂商和半导体公司让 AI 控制设计流程中越来越大的部分，行业正从“人用 AI 工具设计芯片”逐步走向“AI 系统参与设计其后继者所运行的硬件”。不过，机器今天真能设计机器吗？文章认为大概还不能；未来能否做到则是影响深远的大问题。

回顾历史，Cadence、Synopsys、Siemens EDA 以及仿真软件厂商 Ansys 在 2020 年代初、生成式 AI 爆发前就推出了 AI 增强工具。第一代 AI 增强 EDA 主要用机器学习和强化学习解决定义明确的优化问题：给定已有设计、约束和目标，工具可探索大量实现方案，优化布局布线，从而改善功耗、性能和面积（PPA），并缩短开发时间。其关键优势是能从历史运行中学习，用积累数据指导后续设计空间探索，减少满足 PPA 目标所需的迭代次数，有时能产生传统方法需更多工程时间才能得到的结果。但自主性有限：工程师仍需定义约束、配置流程、运行单个工具、分析输出并决定下一步。AI 加速或优化特定阶段，人类仍控制整体设计流程。

最新一代 AI 增强 EDA 工具雄心更大。生成式 AI 可以编写或修改 RTL 与验证代码、分析报告、识别潜在故障点甚至建议修复。更受关注的是 agentic 系统：它们能操作多个 EDA 工具，执行一串工程任务，人工干预非常有限。此类智能体可分析结果、修改设计或参数、启动新的仿真或实现运行、评估结果，并循环执行直到达到指定目标。因此，AI 正从优化 EDA 工具内部的单个步骤，转向自动化芯片开发工作流的一部分。

在企业实践上，2023—2024 年 Cadence 和 Synopsys 均宣布已有数百个芯片设计使用其 AI 增强的 Cadence.ai DSO.ai/VSO.ai/TSO.ai 工具完成。但 Google、Nvidia、OpenAI 和 Architect Labs 代表不同层次的 AI 参与度。Google 的 AlphaChip 主要用强化学习做物理布局规划，放置电路模块并优化布局，并不发明完整设计或架构；Google DeepMind 曾在 2024 年表示 AlphaChip 已用于此前三代 TPU，领先于通用 EDA 行业。Nvidia 更进一步：其内部 AI 系统自动化传统上由硬件工程师完成的工作，并用自有 RTL、文档和独特积累的工程知识训练专用模型，这是商用 EDA 厂商无法获取的数据优势。Nvidia 把其专有 GPU 以及近期 AI 加速器、CPU、DPU、网卡背后的工程数据变成 AI 训练数据，但 Nvidia 仍在自动化和自主芯片设计之间划清界限。

OpenAI 的 Jalapeño 可能是目前最强的“真实硅片”案例。OpenAI 称 AI 直接参与了实现、设计空间探索、验证循环和算术电路优化，使项目从初始设计到流片仅用九个月。在 Hot Chips 会议上，OpenAI 披露了具体 PPA 优势：与人类基线相比，AI 辅助设计使 BF16 乘法器提升 56%，FP4 点积模块提升 21%，FP32 累加器提升 10%，同时使矩阵单元和 SIMD 单元面积分别减少 10% 和 8%。不过 OpenAI 并未称 AI 发明了 Jalapeño 的架构，人类仍负责架构；AI 被广泛用于把架构变成硅片并优化。

Architect Labs 的 Redwood 则在性质上不同。两名人类架构师定义规格后，Architect Labs 称其 AI 自主生成并验证逻辑、生成 RTL、验证并产出固件，还协助开发驱动和内核等软件。不同于 Google、Nvidia 和 OpenAI，该公司明确称其系统执行机器学习协同设计，并表示可探索架构，但未详细说明。Redwood 在不到两周内“产出”，可运行十亿级以上参数模型，但有一个重大保留：它尚未流片，从未作为 ASIC 实际生产；该加速器运行在 FPGA 上，其宣称相对 Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano 的 3.4 倍每瓦性能优势，是基于预计的三星 8LPP 设计。

结论是，几年前 AI 在半导体开发中主要是优化技术，帮工程师更好地实现人类设计；今天它已能生成 RTL、验证设计、操作 EDA 工具甚至探索架构选择，但人类仍定义最终要造什么。这意味着 AI 将显著影响 AI 加速器、GPU/CPU/DPU、网卡和定制 ASIC 等芯片的设计效率，并推动 EDA 从工具自动化走向工作流自动化；然而流片验证、架构意图和最终责任仍掌握在人类手中。我们因此离“机器设计机器”近了很多，却远未到奇点。目前芯片正在帮助设计其继任者，但还远不能决定继任者应该是什么。

items.title: Will Chinese AI companies slow down? A top House Democrat wants answers
items.description:
Image: Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images	

As President Donald Trump prepares to meet tech and AI CEOs in Washington, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) is calling for a treaty between the US and China to keep AI from wreaking havoc on the world. But wrangling leaders in both countries to take action could be a long shot.
In letters shared exclusively with The Verge, Khanna - the top Democrat on the House Select Committee on China and a possible presidential contender - asked a US intelligence agency and Chinese AI companies whether they would be prepared for an incident like OpenAI agents' hack of Hugging Face this summer. The companies included DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI, all of which  …
Read the full story at The Verge.
items.content: As President Donald Trump prepares to meet tech and AI CEOs in Washington, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) is calling for a treaty between the US and China to keep AI from wreaking havoc on the world. But wrangling leaders in both countries to take action could be a long shot.In letters shared exclusively with The Verge, Khanna — the top Democrat on the House Select Committee on China and a possible presidential contender — asked a US intelligence agency and Chinese AI companies whether they would be prepared for an incident like OpenAI agents’ hack of Hugging Face this summer. The companies included DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI, all of which are pursuing high-level artificial intelligence.American and Chinese interests “could not be more different on many issues,” Khanna writes in the letter to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, “but on this discrete concern, it benefits neither country for humanity to lose control of our destiny.”“[I]t benefits neither country for humanity to lose control of our destiny”Khanna requests the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) assess how effectively the US might respond to an AI lab losing control of its bots — a scenario that’s become increasingly common in recent months. Alongside it, he asked the agency to evaluate the Chinese government’s approach to assessing catastrophic AI risks. The information, he says, will help Congress and eventually the White House craft an agreement with their Chinese counterparts.The letters to DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI ask for documentation about their efforts to achieve “superintelligence” and recursive self-improvement (RSI) — a milestone where AI systems can improve on themselves. He asks about any efforts to implement safeguards and “kill switches” for the technology, as well as whether the companies would commit to inspections by a non-governmental agency if a treaty were struck. The companies and ODNI did not immediately respond to requests for comment from The Verge.Khanna’s move follows a meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump at the White House last week. Both men, he says, fail to recognize the risk and urgency around AI. “I think it was constructive that Trump and Xi Jinping at least agreed to talk about AI and have ongoing dialogue about it, but it is not nearly adequate,” Khanna told The Verge in an interview on Monday.He is also skeptical of a planned Tuesday meeting between the White House, House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA), and several American tech executives. “I think it’s an effort to reassure the American people that these tech companies are going to be responsible, and it’s a branding exercise,” Khanna says. “But why should we trust companies that have a motive to maximize profits to be making the rules for what is safe? It’s not that they’re bad people, but would you trust the pharmaceutical executives to determine the rules for what drugs are safe?”“Why should we trust companies that have a motive to maximize profits to be making the rules for what is safe?”Khanna ultimately seeks a US-China treaty banning RSI and monitoring frontier AI labs, but he recognizes that’s unlikely to happen anytime soon. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) has similarly called for an AI treaty between the countries, though Republicans like House China Committee Chair John Moolenaar (R-MI) have been skeptical the Chinese government would keep its end of the bargain. In the meantime, Khanna says he’d like a working group with experts from both countries to suggest safety recommendations and methods for ensuring compliance.But Trump and his allies have been resistant to most regulations or agreements. The morning of his meeting with Xi last week, Trump posted on Truth Social, “Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is. That is China’s position also.” Johnson said on Fox Business that he expected the conversation to revolve around striking “the right balance” of oversight without stifling innovation, warning against losing the AI race against China. Leading US AI companies, however, have called for the US to coordinate with China to slow down the pace of developmentIn the letter to the Chinese AI companies, Khanna acknowledges they’re unlikely to respond in full. He said they didn’t respond to requests in an earlier letter asking for a commitment to slow down AI development alongside OpenAI and Anthropic. Khanna tells The Verge his goal is to “shame them” and “spark a debate” among Chinese AI companies about safety. While he’s critical of US AI firms too, he says, “at least they’re engaging in safety conversations.”Khanna remains confident the US will drive AI safety standards, in part because he believes many Chinese models are distilled from US models. And while world leaders may not recognize the threat, they’re “out of touch with the scientists and technologists in their own countries,” he says. “We need to get the technologists and the engineers who understand this really driving the debate, not CEOs who have a vested interest in making profits, and not politicians who lack a technical expertise and who are more concerned about power.”
items.author: Lauren Feiner
items.titleZh: 中国AI公司会放缓脚步吗？众议院民主党高层想要答案
items.descriptionZh:
美国众议员罗·卡纳（Ro Khanna，加州民主党）在特朗普总统准备于华盛顿会见科技与AI CEO之际，呼吁美中签署一项AI条约，防止AI失控给世界带来灾难。卡纳是众议院中国问题特别委员会民主党首席成员，也被视为可能的总统竞选人。他与 The Verge 独家分享的信件显示，他已分别致信美国国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿，以及中国AI公司 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴和月之暗面（Moonshot AI），询问它们是否准备好应对类似今夏“OpenAI智能体攻击Hugging Face”的事件。三家公司均从事高级AI研发。

在给克莱顿的信中，卡纳承认美中在许多问题上利益“截然不同”，但强调在AI安全这一具体关切上，人类失去对自身命运的控制对两国都没有好处。他要求国家情报总监办公室（ODNI）评估：如果AI实验室失去对其智能体或机器人的控制，美国能多有效应对——这一场景近几个月已越来越常见；同时评估中国政府评估灾难性AI风险的方法。他认为这些信息将帮助国会、并最终帮助白宫与中方谈判协议。

给中国AI公司的信则要求提供其追求“超级智能”和“递归自我改进”（RSI）的文件。RSI指AI系统能够改进自身，被视为可能引发能力快速跃升的关键里程碑；超级智能通常指全面超越人类认知能力的AI系统。卡纳还询问这些公司是否实施保障措施和“终止开关”，以及若达成条约，是否愿意接受非政府机构检查。ODNI 和这些公司未立即回应 The Verge 的置评请求。

此事发生在习近平与特朗普上周在白宫会面之后。卡纳称，两国元首至少同意讨论AI并保持对话，这是建设性的，但远远不够，他认为两人都未充分认识AI风险与紧迫性。他也怀疑周二白宫、众议院议长迈克·约翰逊与多名美国科技高管的会议，称其更像“品牌宣传”，旨在让美国民众相信科技公司会负责任。他质疑为何要信任有利润最大化动机的公司制定安全规则，并用“是否让制药高管决定药物安全规则”作类比。

卡纳的最终目标是推动美中条约，禁止RSI并监督前沿AI实验室，但他承认短期内实现可能性不大。参议员伯尼·桑德斯也呼吁美中达成AI条约，但共和党人、众议院中国委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔等怀疑中国政府会履约。卡纳的替代方案是先建立两国专家工作组，提出安全建议和确保合规的方法。

然而，特朗普及其盟友抵制大多数监管或协议。与习近平会面前，特朗普在 Truth Social 发文称，“超级智能（SI）将是一个重要讨论话题，但我想让它保持现状。中国也是这个立场。”约翰逊在 Fox Business 表示，预期讨论重点是在监督与不扼杀创新之间取得“正确平衡”，并警告不要输掉对华AI竞赛。与此同时，美国领先AI公司呼吁美国与中国协调，以放缓AI开发步伐。

卡纳承认中国AI公司不太可能完整回复，并称早前要求它们与 OpenAI、Anthropic 一起承诺放缓AI开发时，它们也未回应。他说目标是通过公开信“使其难堪”，并在中国AI公司中“引发辩论”。他批评美国AI公司，但认为它们“至少参与了安全对话”。卡纳仍相信美国将推动AI安全标准，部分原因是他认为许多中国模型是从美国模型蒸馏而来，即用大模型输出训练较小模型。他还认为，各国领导人可能未意识到威胁，但与本国科学家和技术专家脱节；应让真正理解问题的技术专家和工程师主导辩论，而不是有利润动机的CEO或缺乏技术专长、更关心权力的政客。

原文未提供具体模型性能参数、算力规模或基准对比数据，讨论主要集中在AI安全治理、中美协调、RSI风险与核查机制。若RSI和超级智能失控，潜在影响将超出实验室，涉及国家安全、经济稳定和人类对技术命运的控制；可能的应用与治理场景包括前沿AI实验室监控、智能体终止开关、跨国条约核查、非政府机构检查及中美专家工作组。

history.title: AI researchers put out videos saying superintelligence is ‘exactly as dangerous as it sounds’
history.description:

Read the full story at The Verge.
history.content: “The chance of human extinction is about a coin flip, in my view,” Geoffrey Irving, a former OpenAI and Google DeepMind employee, said in a new interview. It’s one of a dozen interviews with AI researchers, including current and former employees at OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. Palisade Research, which says it’s a nonprofit studying AIs’ capabilities and motivations, collected and launched the interviews on frominside.ai.Several of the researchers joined Irving in warning about the possibility AI could drive humans extinct. Neel Nanda, a Google DeepMind research scientist, said there’s “at least a 10 percent chance that it causes human extinction, and that is ridiculously high.” We noted comments from both Nanda and Irving in a recent report about the “AI safety” community, and how difficult it is to nail down what that term means, or what anyone should do about it, and even these videos don’t have one cohesive solution to offer.RelatedWe’re running out of reasons to ignore AI safetyInside the suddenly explosive world of AI safetyFormer OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo went as far as claiming that superintelligent AI “would basically be god-like powerful,” and added, “unfortunately we don’t know how to control them at all. And so probably nobody would control them. This is exactly as dangerous as it sounds and must not be allowed to happen.”While each video is available in full, the site also collects segments from multiple people speaking on similar topics, including whether this is all just hype or marketing, and why they would work on something that they believe is this dangerous. Some of the responses include Google’s Mary Phuong saying “I think you absolutely should be suspicious of what I’m saying because I am being paid by the lab,” and Nanda’s explanation that “If I did not believe that my work was directly reducing these existential risks, I would quit… These companies are not going to stop making these systems just because I quit.”
history.author: Stevie Bonifield
history.titleZh: AI研究人员发布视频称超级智能“危险程度恰如其名”
history.descriptionZh:
前OpenAI和Google DeepMind员工杰弗里·欧文（Geoffrey Irving）在接受采访时称，在他看来，人类因AI而灭绝的概率“大约像掷硬币”，即约一半。这是Palisade Research在frominside.ai发布的一系列AI研究员访谈之一。Palisade自称非营利组织，研究AI的能力与动机；访谈对象有十几位，包括OpenAI、Google和Anthropic的现任及前任员工。多名受访者与欧文一样警告AI可能导致人类灭绝。Google DeepMind研究科学家尼尔·南达（Neel Nanda）说，AI造成人类灭绝的概率“至少10%，这高得离谱”。相关报道也提到，AI安全社区内部对“AI安全”的定义、该做什么缺乏共识，这些视频同样没有给出统一答案。

前OpenAI研究员丹尼尔·科科塔伊洛（Daniel Kokotajlo）称，超级智能AI“基本上会像神一样强大”，而人类“根本不知道如何控制它们”，“所以很可能没人能控制它们。这正和听起来一样危险，绝不能被允许发生”。从技术层面看，这组访谈的核心并非新模型或算法创新，而是AI安全中的控制/对齐难题：当系统能力远超人类时，如何保证其受控。网站除完整视频外，还按主题汇集多人发言，讨论这些警告是否只是炒作或营销，以及他们为何要从事自己认为如此危险的工作。

对于利益冲突，Google的玛丽·芳（Mary Phuong）说：“你绝对应该怀疑我说的话，因为我拿实验室的工资。”南达则解释：“如果我不相信我的工作能直接降低这些存在性风险，我会辞职……但这些公司不会因为我辞职就停止制造这些系统。”文章关联内容还指出，人们越来越没有理由忽视AI安全，AI安全领域突然成为热点，但其含义、责任和解决方案仍高度模糊。

history.title: Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond
history.description: How close is AI to designing the very same chips it runs on? We explore how artificial intelligence is being used in modern chip design today.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter In late August, Architect Labs claimed it had designed a chip that was almost entirely developed by AI, an industry-first achievement. AI is already used to optimize floorplans, placement and routing, verification, and other stages of semiconductor development. Generative AI can assist engineers with RTL code, whereas emerging agentic systems can operate electronic design automation (EDA) tools, analyze results, identify problems, modify designs, and repeat the process with increasingly less human intervention. Meanwhile, human engineers still define and develop architectures and make fundamental design decisions that determine what a chip does and how it works.This creates a curious feedback loop. Today's AI models run on processors designed by human engineers with growing assistance from AI; those models can then help design more capable processors for the next generation of AI systems. As EDA vendors and semiconductor companies give AI control over progressively larger portions of the design process, the industry is gradually moving from humans using AI tools to design chips toward AI systems participating in the design of the hardware on which their successors will run.Can machines indeed design machines today? Probably not. But will they be able to do so in the future? That's a big question with important ramifications — and engineers have been pondering it for longer than you might think.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: A brief history of AI in chip developmentCadence, Synopsys, and Siemens EDA, all leading developers of EDA software, alongside Ansys — a leading designer of simulation software — rolled out AI-enhanced versions of their tools in the early 2020s, before the generative AI boom took the world by storm. (Image credit: Synopsys)The first generation of AI-enhanced EDA software primarily used machine learning (ML) and reinforcement learning (RL) to tackle well-defined optimization problems. Given an existing design, a set of constraints, and particular targets, these tools could explore numerous implementation options to optimize placement and routing, and therefore power, performance, and area (PPA), while shrinking development time. Essentially, AI could find a better way to implement a design, but the design itself and its goals were still defined by engineers. You may like Hot Chips 2026: OpenAI's Jalapeño AI ASIC unpacked OpenAI Jalapeño design interview transcript Synopsys debuts Autopilot platform for developing chips autonomously using AI One of the key advantages of these tools was their ability to learn from previous runs and use accumulated data to guide subsequent design-space exploration, something which could reduce the number of iterations needed to meet PPA targets and, in some cases, produce results that would have required considerably more engineering time using conventional methods. Yet the autonomy of these tools is limited, as engineers define constraints, configure flows, run individual tools, analyze their output, and decide what to try next. AI accelerates or optimizes particular stages of chip development, but humans still control the overall design flow. And that's changing with newer generations.The latest AI-enhanced EDA tools are considerably more ambitious. Generative AI can write or modify RTL and verification code, analyze reports, identify potential points of failure, and even suggest fixes. Meanwhile, emerging agentic systems can operate multiple EDA tools and execute sequences of engineering tasks with very limited human intervention. Such an agent can analyze results, modify a design or its parameters, launch another simulation or implementation run, evaluate the outcome, and repeat the process until it reaches specified targets. As a result, AI is gradually moving from optimizing individual steps inside EDA tools to automating parts of the chip development workflow itself.From big bang to architecturesIn 2023 – 2024, both Cadence and Synopsys announced that hundreds of chip designs have been completed using their AI-enhanced Cadence.ai DSO.ai/VSO.ai/TSO.ai tools. Moreover, leading high-tech companies revealed details about how they used AI to complete their projects. Yet putting Google, Nvidia, OpenAI, and Architect Labs into the same bucket is not right, as they represent different degrees of AI involvement in chip development. (Image credit: Google Deepmind)Google, which was among the first high-tech giants to announce the use of AI to develop its AI accelerators, seems to be the least radical. Google's AlphaChip uses reinforcement learning mostly for physical floorplanning: it places circuit blocks and optimizes layouts, but it does not invent the entire design or the architecture itself. Google DeepMind said in 2024 that AlphaChip had been used for the previous three generations of TPUs, meaning Google was well ahead of the general EDA industry with its tools. (The company has not shared AlphaChip's progress in detail since then.)Nvidia is more interesting because its internal AI systems tend to automate work traditionally performed by hardware engineers. The important distinction is that Nvidia trains specialized models on its own RTL, documentation, and unique accumulated engineering knowledge, something a merchant EDA vendor cannot access. This makes Nvidia an example of a chip designer that turns the engineering data behind its proprietary GPU and, more recently, AI accelerator, CPU, DPU, and network cards into training data for AI. Nonetheless, Nvidia itself draws a clear line between its automation and autonomous chip design. What to read next Anthropic co-designing custom AI inference chips to bypass costly Nvidia GPUs OpenAI says its next-generation processors could be made at Samsung Hot Chips 2026: Cerebras lays out the future of wafer-scale AI OpenAI's Jalapeño is probably the strongest real-silicon example we currently have. OpenAI says AI was directly involved in implementation, design-space exploration, verification loops, and arithmetic-circuit optimization, which enabled the company to go from initial design to tapeout in nine months. At Hot Chips, OpenAI disclosed some concrete PPA advantages: Compared with human baselines, AI-assisted designs improved a BF16 multiplier by 56%, an FP4 dot-product block by 21%, and an FP32 accumulator by 10%, while reducing the area of matrix and SIMD units by 10% and 8%, respectively.OpenAI has not said that AI invented Jalapeño's architecture, so humans have indeed remained responsible for it. But AI was extensively used to turn that architecture into silicon and optimize it ... which brings us to Architect Labs.Indeed, Architect Labs' Redwood is qualitatively different. Two human architects defined the specification, after which Architect Labs says its AI autonomously generated and verified the logic, generated RTL, verified it, and produced firmware. To top it off, AI also assisted software development, including drivers and kernels. Meanwhile, unlike Google, Nvidia, and OpenAI, the company explicitly describes its system as one that performs machine learning co-design and says it can explore architectures, though without elaboration.Redwood was 'produced' in under two weeks and runs billion-plus-parameter models, but there is a huge caveat: It has not been taped out. It has never actually been produced as an ASIC; the accelerator runs on an FPGA, and the claimed 3.4X performance-per-watt advantage over Nvidia's Jetson Orin Nano is based on a projected Samsung 8LPP design.Final wordsJust a few years ago, AI in semiconductor development was largely an optimization technology that helped engineers find better ways to implement designs created by humans. Today, it can generate RTL, verify designs, operate EDA tools, and even explore architectural choices, although humans still define what ultimately gets built.We are therefore considerably closer to machines designing machines, but nowhere near the singularity quite yet. For now, chips are helping design their successors. But they aren't even close to deciding what those successors should be.
history.author: Anton Shilov
history.titleZh: 硅开始设计硅——人工智能如何从EDA工具到OpenAI的Jalapeño乃至更广领域应用于芯片制造
history.descriptionZh:
8月底，Architect Labs 宣称其设计了一款几乎完全由 AI 开发的芯片，并称这是业界首次。围绕这一事件，文章指出 AI 在芯片开发中的角色正从辅助优化走向更深入参与。AI 早已用于优化芯片的 Floorplan、布局布线、验证等环节；生成式 AI 可帮助编写 RTL 代码；新兴的 agentic 系统则可操作 EDA 工具、分析结果、发现问题、修改设计并反复迭代，人工干预越来越少。但人类工程师仍负责定义架构和决定芯片功能与工作方式。由此形成反馈循环：今天的 AI 模型运行在人类工程师借助 AI 设计的处理器上，这些模型又能帮助设计下一代 AI 系统所需的更强处理器。随着 EDA 厂商和半导体公司让 AI 控制设计流程中越来越大的部分，行业正从“人用 AI 工具设计芯片”逐步走向“AI 系统参与设计其后继者所运行的硬件”。不过，机器今天真能设计机器吗？文章认为大概还不能；未来能否做到则是影响深远的大问题。

回顾历史，Cadence、Synopsys、Siemens EDA 以及仿真软件厂商 Ansys 在 2020 年代初、生成式 AI 爆发前就推出了 AI 增强工具。第一代 AI 增强 EDA 主要用机器学习和强化学习解决定义明确的优化问题：给定已有设计、约束和目标，工具可探索大量实现方案，优化布局布线，从而改善功耗、性能和面积（PPA），并缩短开发时间。其关键优势是能从历史运行中学习，用积累数据指导后续设计空间探索，减少满足 PPA 目标所需的迭代次数，有时能产生传统方法需更多工程时间才能得到的结果。但自主性有限：工程师仍需定义约束、配置流程、运行单个工具、分析输出并决定下一步。AI 加速或优化特定阶段，人类仍控制整体设计流程。

最新一代 AI 增强 EDA 工具雄心更大。生成式 AI 可以编写或修改 RTL 与验证代码、分析报告、识别潜在故障点甚至建议修复。更受关注的是 agentic 系统：它们能操作多个 EDA 工具，执行一串工程任务，人工干预非常有限。此类智能体可分析结果、修改设计或参数、启动新的仿真或实现运行、评估结果，并循环执行直到达到指定目标。因此，AI 正从优化 EDA 工具内部的单个步骤，转向自动化芯片开发工作流的一部分。

在企业实践上，2023—2024 年 Cadence 和 Synopsys 均宣布已有数百个芯片设计使用其 AI 增强的 Cadence.ai DSO.ai/VSO.ai/TSO.ai 工具完成。但 Google、Nvidia、OpenAI 和 Architect Labs 代表不同层次的 AI 参与度。Google 的 AlphaChip 主要用强化学习做物理布局规划，放置电路模块并优化布局，并不发明完整设计或架构；Google DeepMind 曾在 2024 年表示 AlphaChip 已用于此前三代 TPU，领先于通用 EDA 行业。Nvidia 更进一步：其内部 AI 系统自动化传统上由硬件工程师完成的工作，并用自有 RTL、文档和独特积累的工程知识训练专用模型，这是商用 EDA 厂商无法获取的数据优势。Nvidia 把其专有 GPU 以及近期 AI 加速器、CPU、DPU、网卡背后的工程数据变成 AI 训练数据，但 Nvidia 仍在自动化和自主芯片设计之间划清界限。

OpenAI 的 Jalapeño 可能是目前最强的“真实硅片”案例。OpenAI 称 AI 直接参与了实现、设计空间探索、验证循环和算术电路优化，使项目从初始设计到流片仅用九个月。在 Hot Chips 会议上，OpenAI 披露了具体 PPA 优势：与人类基线相比，AI 辅助设计使 BF16 乘法器提升 56%，FP4 点积模块提升 21%，FP32 累加器提升 10%，同时使矩阵单元和 SIMD 单元面积分别减少 10% 和 8%。不过 OpenAI 并未称 AI 发明了 Jalapeño 的架构，人类仍负责架构；AI 被广泛用于把架构变成硅片并优化。

Architect Labs 的 Redwood 则在性质上不同。两名人类架构师定义规格后，Architect Labs 称其 AI 自主生成并验证逻辑、生成 RTL、验证并产出固件，还协助开发驱动和内核等软件。不同于 Google、Nvidia 和 OpenAI，该公司明确称其系统执行机器学习协同设计，并表示可探索架构，但未详细说明。Redwood 在不到两周内“产出”，可运行十亿级以上参数模型，但有一个重大保留：它尚未流片，从未作为 ASIC 实际生产；该加速器运行在 FPGA 上，其宣称相对 Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano 的 3.4 倍每瓦性能优势，是基于预计的三星 8LPP 设计。

结论是，几年前 AI 在半导体开发中主要是优化技术，帮工程师更好地实现人类设计；今天它已能生成 RTL、验证设计、操作 EDA 工具甚至探索架构选择，但人类仍定义最终要造什么。这意味着 AI 将显著影响 AI 加速器、GPU/CPU/DPU、网卡和定制 ASIC 等芯片的设计效率，并推动 EDA 从工具自动化走向工作流自动化；然而流片验证、架构意图和最终责任仍掌握在人类手中。我们因此离“机器设计机器”近了很多，却远未到奇点。目前芯片正在帮助设计其继任者，但还远不能决定继任者应该是什么。

history.title: Will Chinese AI companies slow down? A top House Democrat wants answers
history.description:
Image: Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images	

As President Donald Trump prepares to meet tech and AI CEOs in Washington, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) is calling for a treaty between the US and China to keep AI from wreaking havoc on the world. But wrangling leaders in both countries to take action could be a long shot.

Read the full story at The Verge.
history.content: As President Donald Trump prepares to meet tech and AI CEOs in Washington, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) is calling for a treaty between the US and China to keep AI from wreaking havoc on the world. But wrangling leaders in both countries to take action could be a long shot.In letters shared exclusively with The Verge, Khanna — the top Democrat on the House Select Committee on China and a possible presidential contender — asked a US intelligence agency and Chinese AI companies whether they would be prepared for an incident like OpenAI agents’ hack of Hugging Face this summer. The companies included DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI, all of which are pursuing high-level artificial intelligence.American and Chinese interests “could not be more different on many issues,” Khanna writes in the letter to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, “but on this discrete concern, it benefits neither country for humanity to lose control of our destiny.”“[I]t benefits neither country for humanity to lose control of our destiny”Khanna requests the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) assess how effectively the US might respond to an AI lab losing control of its bots — a scenario that’s become increasingly common in recent months. Alongside it, he asked the agency to evaluate the Chinese government’s approach to assessing catastrophic AI risks. The information, he says, will help Congress and eventually the White House craft an agreement with their Chinese counterparts.The letters to DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI ask for documentation about their efforts to achieve “superintelligence” and recursive self-improvement (RSI) — a milestone where AI systems can improve on themselves. He asks about any efforts to implement safeguards and “kill switches” for the technology, as well as whether the companies would commit to inspections by a non-governmental agency if a treaty were struck. The companies and ODNI did not immediately respond to requests for comment from The Verge.Khanna’s move follows a meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump at the White House last week. Both men, he says, fail to recognize the risk and urgency around AI. “I think it was constructive that Trump and Xi Jinping at least agreed to talk about AI and have ongoing dialogue about it, but it is not nearly adequate,” Khanna told The Verge in an interview on Monday.He is also skeptical of a planned Tuesday meeting between the White House, House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA), and several American tech executives. “I think it’s an effort to reassure the American people that these tech companies are going to be responsible, and it’s a branding exercise,” Khanna says. “But why should we trust companies that have a motive to maximize profits to be making the rules for what is safe? It’s not that they’re bad people, but would you trust the pharmaceutical executives to determine the rules for what drugs are safe?”“Why should we trust companies that have a motive to maximize profits to be making the rules for what is safe?”Khanna ultimately seeks a US-China treaty banning RSI and monitoring frontier AI labs, but he recognizes that’s unlikely to happen anytime soon. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) has similarly called for an AI treaty between the countries, though Republicans like House China Committee Chair John Moolenaar (R-MI) have been skeptical the Chinese government would keep its end of the bargain. In the meantime, Khanna says he’d like a working group with experts from both countries to suggest safety recommendations and methods for ensuring compliance.But Trump and his allies have been resistant to most regulations or agreements. The morning of his meeting with Xi last week, Trump posted on Truth Social, “Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is. That is China’s position also.” Johnson said on Fox Business that he expected the conversation to revolve around striking “the right balance” of oversight without stifling innovation, warning against losing the AI race against China. Leading US AI companies, however, have called for the US to coordinate with China to slow down the pace of developmentIn the letter to the Chinese AI companies, Khanna acknowledges they’re unlikely to respond in full. He said they didn’t respond to requests in an earlier letter asking for a commitment to slow down AI development alongside OpenAI and Anthropic. Khanna tells The Verge his goal is to “shame them” and “spark a debate” among Chinese AI companies about safety. While he’s critical of US AI firms too, he says, “at least they’re engaging in safety conversations.”Khanna remains confident the US will drive AI safety standards, in part because he believes many Chinese models are distilled from US models. And while world leaders may not recognize the threat, they’re “out of touch with the scientists and technologists in their own countries,” he says. “We need to get the technologists and the engineers who understand this really driving the debate, not CEOs who have a vested interest in making profits, and not politicians who lack a technical expertise and who are more concerned about power.”

history.titleZh: 中国AI公司会放缓脚步吗？众议院民主党高层想要答案
history.descriptionZh:
美国众议员罗·卡纳（Ro Khanna，加州民主党）在特朗普总统准备于华盛顿会见科技与AI CEO之际，呼吁美中签署一项AI条约，防止AI失控给世界带来灾难。卡纳是众议院中国问题特别委员会民主党首席成员，也被视为可能的总统竞选人。他与 The Verge 独家分享的信件显示，他已分别致信美国国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿，以及中国AI公司 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴和月之暗面（Moonshot AI），询问它们是否准备好应对类似今夏“OpenAI智能体攻击Hugging Face”的事件。三家公司均从事高级AI研发。

在给克莱顿的信中，卡纳承认美中在许多问题上利益“截然不同”，但强调在AI安全这一具体关切上，人类失去对自身命运的控制对两国都没有好处。他要求国家情报总监办公室（ODNI）评估：如果AI实验室失去对其智能体或机器人的控制，美国能多有效应对——这一场景近几个月已越来越常见；同时评估中国政府评估灾难性AI风险的方法。他认为这些信息将帮助国会、并最终帮助白宫与中方谈判协议。

给中国AI公司的信则要求提供其追求“超级智能”和“递归自我改进”（RSI）的文件。RSI指AI系统能够改进自身，被视为可能引发能力快速跃升的关键里程碑；超级智能通常指全面超越人类认知能力的AI系统。卡纳还询问这些公司是否实施保障措施和“终止开关”，以及若达成条约，是否愿意接受非政府机构检查。ODNI 和这些公司未立即回应 The Verge 的置评请求。

此事发生在习近平与特朗普上周在白宫会面之后。卡纳称，两国元首至少同意讨论AI并保持对话，这是建设性的，但远远不够，他认为两人都未充分认识AI风险与紧迫性。他也怀疑周二白宫、众议院议长迈克·约翰逊与多名美国科技高管的会议，称其更像“品牌宣传”，旨在让美国民众相信科技公司会负责任。他质疑为何要信任有利润最大化动机的公司制定安全规则，并用“是否让制药高管决定药物安全规则”作类比。

卡纳的最终目标是推动美中条约，禁止RSI并监督前沿AI实验室，但他承认短期内实现可能性不大。参议员伯尼·桑德斯也呼吁美中达成AI条约，但共和党人、众议院中国委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔等怀疑中国政府会履约。卡纳的替代方案是先建立两国专家工作组，提出安全建议和确保合规的方法。

然而，特朗普及其盟友抵制大多数监管或协议。与习近平会面前，特朗普在 Truth Social 发文称，“超级智能（SI）将是一个重要讨论话题，但我想让它保持现状。中国也是这个立场。”约翰逊在 Fox Business 表示，预期讨论重点是在监督与不扼杀创新之间取得“正确平衡”，并警告不要输掉对华AI竞赛。与此同时，美国领先AI公司呼吁美国与中国协调，以放缓AI开发步伐。

卡纳承认中国AI公司不太可能完整回复，并称早前要求它们与 OpenAI、Anthropic 一起承诺放缓AI开发时，它们也未回应。他说目标是通过公开信“使其难堪”，并在中国AI公司中“引发辩论”。他批评美国AI公司，但认为它们“至少参与了安全对话”。卡纳仍相信美国将推动AI安全标准，部分原因是他认为许多中国模型是从美国模型蒸馏而来，即用大模型输出训练较小模型。他还认为，各国领导人可能未意识到威胁，但与本国科学家和技术专家脱节；应让真正理解问题的技术专家和工程师主导辩论，而不是有利润动机的CEO或缺乏技术专长、更关心权力的政客。

原文未提供具体模型性能参数、算力规模或基准对比数据，讨论主要集中在AI安全治理、中美协调、RSI风险与核查机制。若RSI和超级智能失控，潜在影响将超出实验室，涉及国家安全、经济稳定和人类对技术命运的控制；可能的应用与治理场景包括前沿AI实验室监控、智能体终止开关、跨国条约核查、非政府机构检查及中美专家工作组。
